slice: Recognize both floating zero signs in non-ANSI safe divisors and NULLIFZERO

scope.runtime: Two planner files. A small native SparkNullIfZero UDF reuses DataFusion IsZeroFunc and Arrow nullif, changing validity while preserving type and sharing value buffers. Scalar zeros become typed NULL; other scalars pass through.
scope.callers: The non-ANSI floating branch of make_safe_divisor, shared by /, DIV and %, and floating NULLIFZERO in both ANSI modes. Spark rejects floating DIV; missing input type validation remains recorded.

corpus.origin: Local pre-implementation matrix of FLOAT/DOUBLE operators, NULLIFZERO and controls. All 120 original SQL shapes are retained, including 60 observations in both ANSI modes demonstrating missing rejection of floating DIV. Not an upstream CI list.

provenance.implementation_origin: Local planner adapter using installed Arrow 58.4.0 and DataFusion 54.1.0. No additional Sail code was imported and no upstream PR is claimed to supply this fix.

post_verification_import_order.post_verification_change: Moved the single SparkNullIfZero import to rustfmt order. Removing that import from compiled and final sources gives byte-identical files. No executable code changed.

limitations: Prior corpora retain four original, twenty ROUND and sixty-five floating division value/type or error-stage differences, plus five recorded same-stage error-cause differences.

New coverage retains eighty-four differences: sixty floating DIV type rejection observations, twenty ANSI remainder observations, two ANSI division/LIMIT 0 observations and two generic NULLIF observations. These are repeated query shapes and modes, not eighty-four distinct bugs. Invalid floating DIV results may change through the shared helper, but they remain mismatches because Spark rejects the types.

Numeric comparison checks exact ordered numeric values, types and coarse error stage, not full schema metadata or structured error conditions. Focused checks add thirty-seven new error causes and two ZEROIFNULL signed-zero outputs, preserving all 149 prior checks. Delta comparison separately checks names, nullability and metadata.

Float64 division execution is measured. Float planning, Float32 execution, remainder and standalone NULLIFZERO are not separately timed. The four existing controls have separate planning and execution measurements.

CPU frequency is not fixed and the host is not isolated. Small timing differences do not establish zero overhead. The default-allocator ROUND median changes by +23.34%; a diagnostic with fixed thresholds gives +0.52% with effectively identical instructions. Both are retained; no production allocator setting changes.
